cards.explanation: The answer is the temple courts, friends. John says Jesus "…found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables." right in the temple courts (John 2:14). Picture setting up a cash register and a pen of sheep where people came to worship. That's a lot of stuff in one courtyard.
The answer is whip, friends. John says Jesus "…made a whip out of cords…" (John 2:15). Cords in, whip out. I couldn't build anything useful from a pile of cords, so I admire the skill.

The answer is True. John says Jesus "…drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle." (John 2:15). The sheep and cattle are named right there in the verse. I bet that was a LOUD moment, with hooves going everywhere.

The answer is that He pours out their coins and overturns the tables. John says Jesus "…poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables." (John 2:15). Coins everywhere, tables flipped. I bet those coins made quite a racket.

The answer is marketplace, friends! Jesus says, "How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!" (John 2:16). Now hear the words "…My Father’s house…" A HOUSE, bakers! Nobody sets up a cash register on a stranger's couch, and this house is His Father's.

The answer is zeal for God's house. The disciples remember it is written, "Zeal for Your house will consume Me." (John 2:17). Zeal means a burning care for something. They watch Jesus act and the verse comes to their minds.

The answer is a sign to prove His authority. The Jews demanded, "What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?" (John 2:18). They want proof for what He just did. Notice they ask for a sign, not an apology.

The answer is forty-six, friends. The Jews say, "This temple took forty-six years to build…" (John 2:20). That's a long time to build something. I think hearing someone talk about three days sounded wild to them.
The answer is the temple of His body, and that's the twist. John tells us, "…Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body." (John 2:21). The Jews heard a building. Jesus meant Himself.

The answer is after He was raised from the dead. John says, "After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this." (John 2:22). That's when the memory comes up, after the resurrection. Then, "…they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken." (John 2:22).
The answer is believe, friends. John says many people saw the signs "…and believed in His name." (John 2:23). The signs got their attention, and they believed. Keep that in mind for the next verse.

The answer is False. John says, "…Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all." (John 2:24). Many people believed in His name, yet He didn't entrust Himself to them. That's a surprise, and the text just tells us plainly.

The answer is because He knew them all. That's the reason John gives: "…Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all." (John 2:24). Verse 25 adds that He "…did not need any testimony about man…" (John 2:25). The reason is right there in the text.
